blurb: twelve cases for the world’s only consulting detective, from his rooms at 221B Baker Street.
source: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes by Arthur Conan Doyle (1892). Read it in your own copy, or borrow it free from your library.

streets.name: A Scandal in Bohemia
streets.blurb: A king needs a photograph back, and only Holmes can find where Irene Adler has hidden it.
streets.how: Look round Irene Adler’s sitting-room, then say where the photograph is hidden.

params.objective: Work out where the photograph is hidden

clues.label: The window
clues.text: Watson throws a smoke-rocket through the window, and the cry goes up: “Fire!”

clues.label: The bell-pull
clues.text: When she thought the house was on fire, Irene Adler rushed straight to a spot just above the right bell-pull.

clues.label: The sofa
clues.text: Holmes, dressed as a clergyman, was carried in and laid on the sofa — the perfect place to watch.

solve.label: The hiding place
options: In a recess behind a sliding panel above the right bell-pull
solve.hint: Where did she rush when she thought the house was on fire?

streets.name: The Red-Headed League
streets.blurb: A pawnbroker is paid to copy out an encyclopaedia — while someone digs under his shop.
streets.how: Creep through the dark bank cellar to your hiding place by the crates without the lantern-light catching you.

params.objective: Reach the crates without being seen

streets.name: A Case of Identity
streets.blurb: Miss Mary Sutherland’s fiancé vanished on their wedding morning.
streets.how: Look at the letters and the typewriter, then work out who Hosmer Angel really was.

params.objective: Work out who Hosmer Angel really was

clues.label: Hosmer’s letters
clues.text: Every letter is typewritten — even the signature.

clues.label: The typewriter
clues.text: A typewriter has little quirks: one letter slurred, another with no tail. Hosmer’s letters have exactly the same quirks as notes from Mr. Windibank.

clues.label: The description
clues.text: Hosmer wore tinted glasses and whiskers, and only ever met Mary in the evening. Her stepfather was always away “abroad” when Hosmer came.

solve.label: The answer
options: Her stepfather, Mr. Windibank, in disguise
A real man who ran away to sea

streets.name: The Boscombe Valley Mystery
streets.blurb: A man is found by the Boscombe Pool, and his son is accused.
streets.how: Search the ground round the pool for six sets of footprints.

params.label: footprints
params.objective: Find the footprints round the pool

finale.say: Here are three separate tracks of the same feet — and a fourth. A tall man, left-footed, with a limp…

streets.name: The Five Orange Pips
streets.blurb: A young man brings Holmes an envelope that held five dried orange pips.
streets.how: Look at the envelopes and their postmarks, then work out how the senders were travelling.

params.objective: Work out how the senders travelled

clues.label: The map
clues.text: Pondicherry, Dundee, London — every one of them a seaport. And there were weeks between the letters.

solve.label: Holmes’s deduction
options: By sailing-ship, from port to port
solve.hint: What do all three postmarks have in common?

streets.name: The Man with the Twisted Lip
streets.blurb: Neville St. Clair has vanished, and a beggar called Hugh Boone was in the room where he was last seen.
streets.how: Look round the room by the river, then work out who the beggar really is.

params.objective: Work out who Hugh Boone really is

clues.label: The window
clues.text: Mrs. St. Clair saw her husband at this window — and then he was gone.

clues.label: The coat
clues.text: Neville St. Clair’s coat, its pockets stuffed with pennies and halfpennies.

clues.label: Holmes’s bag
clues.text: Holmes has brought a very large bath-sponge.

solve.label: The beggar
solve.prompt: Who is the beggar Hugh Boone?
options: A thief who stole the coat
solve.hint: What will happen when Holmes uses the sponge?

streets.name: The Blue Carbuncle
streets.blurb: A precious blue stone turns up inside a Christmas goose.
streets.how: Race through London and pick up the trail of goose feathers — find at least four before the end.

params.objective: Follow the goose trail across London

streets.name: The Speckled Band
streets.blurb: Helen Stoner is afraid of the same fate as her sister, and of a strange whistle in the night.
streets.how: Slip through the dark grounds to the bell-pull in the bedroom without being seen.

params.objective: Reach the bell-pull without being seen

streets.name: The Engineer's Thumb
streets.blurb: An engineer is called out at night to look at a machine — and finds himself in great danger.
streets.how: Run! Get out of the press-room and away before the Colonel catches you.

streets.name: The Noble Bachelor
streets.blurb: Lord St. Simon’s bride has vanished from the wedding breakfast.
streets.how: Gather the six clues the bride left behind.

streets.name: The Beryl Coronet
streets.blurb: A banker’s priceless coronet is damaged in the night, and his son is blamed.
streets.how: Follow the footprints across the snowy garden.

params.label: footprints
params.objective: Read the story written in the snow

streets.name: The Copper Beeches
streets.blurb: A governess is paid well to cut her hair and wear an electric-blue dress — and told never to go into one wing of the house.
streets.how: Sneak past Mr. Rucastle to the door of the locked wing.

skyRun.name: The Rooftop Chase
skyRun.blurb: a chase across London’s rooftops and chimney pots.
skyRun.how: Leap from chimney stack to chimney stack, up over the rooftops of London.

params.done: All London lies below you in the fog.

npcs.name: Wiggins
npcs.idle: The Baker Street Irregulars, at your service!
npcs.thanks: Holmes says you’re the best Irregular we’ve had.

npcs.name: Mrs. Hudson
npcs.idle: Mr. Holmes is out, dear. He usually is.

npcs.name: Inspector Lestrade
npcs.idle: Holmes again? Well, he does have his uses.

steps.text: Talk to Wiggins outside 221B Baker Street.
steps.say: Mr. Holmes has three messages to go out, sharp. I’ve dropped ’em in the street, ain’t I! Find all three and deliver them for me?

steps.text: Find Mr. Holmes’s three messages around Baker Street.
Deliver each message: Mrs. Hudson, Inspector Lestrade and the cabman.

steps.say: All three? You’re quick! Here’s your shilling — well, your coins.

vault.name: 221B Baker Street
vault.blurb: an escape room in Holmes’s sitting-room, testing all twelve cases.
vault.intro: Holmes has locked the sitting-room door and left you three locks to open. “You know my methods, Watson. Apply them.”

stations.label: Holmes’s scrapbook
stations.lock: Lock 1 · The clue that cracked it
stations.text: Each page holds a case. Match each one to the clue that cracked it.
stations.lesson: Holmes notices the one small thing everyone else ignores.

solve.prompt: Match each case to its clue.
pairs: A bell-rope that rings no bell
solve.hint: Think about the one strange detail in each case.

stations.label: The last case
stations.text: Mrs. Hudson’s silver teapot has vanished from 221B! The ransom note is typewritten — even the signature. Deep footmarks in the snow outside the window show someone stood there a long time. The only typewriter in the house belongs to the lodger upstairs, who “never goes out”.
stations.lesson: Like Holmes: put the small clues together, and the answer is “simplicity itself”.

solve.hint: Whose typewriter is it? Someone who “never goes out” stood in the snow…

vault.outro: You know his methods — and you applied them.
